title: Privileged data paths and pricing approval roundtable
topics: pricing approval timeline and egress fees
summary: Procurement and legal stakeholders from Sable Health walked through required contract controls (DPA/MSA), keyed on data-paths for PHI-like telemetry, and asked for clarifications on VPC/private deploy options, KMS integrations, and pricing line-items (egress, reserved capacity). Redwood clarified SLA tiers, pilot footprint, and next steps: share redlined MSA, security pack, and a benchmark plan for a 2-week pilot. Action items captured below.
action_items: Priya (Sable) - Provide list of mandatory DPA clauses and any non-negotiable data residency language; due 2026-06-08
Maya (Redwood) - Send redwood standard MSA + annotated DPA and SOC2 attestation bundle; due 2026-06-03
Liam (Redwood) - Draft pilot benchmarking plan (latency, throughput, token-cost spreadsheet) and runbook for VPC onboarding; due 2026-06-05
Devon (Sable) - Share sample traffic profile and actual sequence length distribution for pilot (csv); due 2026-06-04
Marcus (Sable) - Confirm KMS requirements (bring-your-own-key vs. Redwood-managed) and list of blocked ciphers; due 2026-06-09
next_steps: Redwood to circulate security pack and annotated MSA/DPA within 48 hours
Schedule technical onboarding working session (SE + Sable infra) for week of 2026-06-07
Procurement to route pricing approval once pilot numbers are agreed
Set up a 2-week dedicated pilot on a small GPU pool with agreed SLOs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-01 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Anya (Head of Procurement), Marcus (CISO), Priya (Legal), Devon (Platform)

Summary (auto): procurement and security focus; pilot and pricing next steps discussed.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side — I'm Maya, account exec, and i have Liam our SE here. how's everyone?
[00:18] Anya (Sable): Hi all, thanks. we're trying to move this through procurement this quarter, so want to make sure contract and security bits lined up.
[00:28] Marcus (Sable): Yeah, hi. i'm Marcus, i'm the CISO — main concerns: PHI-like telemetry, keying, and where tokens flow. we need to understand VPC option very clearly.
[00:39] Maya (Redwood): absolutely. we'll aim to map the data path and show the private deployment options. Liam, do you want to cover architecture?
[00:45] Liam (Redwood): sure. so at a high level, Redwood runs three deployment modes — hosted API, dedicated capacity, and private (VPC/on-prem). for sensitive workloads the VPC private runtime keeps customer traffic inside the customer's VPC and optional customer KMS for keys. there's a few flavours though — bring-your-own-key with HSM, or Redwood-managed KMS integration.
[01:12] Priya (Sable): pause — is that first hop encrypted? like TLS between caller and edge? also egress paths? we're obligated to minimize cross-border transfers.
[01:23] Liam (Redwood): yes TLS in transit. for private deployments, traffic never leaves the VPC except for control-plane signals which are minimized and can be routed via a private peering if needed. that said, there are some places where logs or telemetry may be optionally forwarded; we can turn that off.
[01:45] Devon (Sable): can you be specific on what "control-plane signals" are? we need to know whether any user data is sent back to redwood for billing or diagnostics.
[01:55] Liam (Redwood): yes — control-plane is scheduling, health checks, and metrics. by default anonymized metrics are sent; full request payloads are not sent. for customers on private we can disable any payload telemetry and only send aggregated metrics.
[02:12] Marcus (Sable): ok good. and about KMS: we have strict key custody. we prefer BYOK with HSM and FIPS-validated ciphers. can Redwood support that?
[02:24] Liam (Redwood): we do support BYOK through standard KMS integrations and can wire to customer HSM in many cases. we'll need to capture exact ciphers — if you send an inventory we can validate.
[02:36] Maya (Redwood): Priya, on the DPA/MSA — what are your must-haves? any non-negotiables?
[02:43] Priya (Sable): indemnity cap adjustments, stronger audit log retention clauses, and explicit data residency language. also need SOC2 plus penetration test reports, and an SLA defined for token-level latency and uptime. we also ask for a breach notification window of 72 hours.
[02:58] Maya (Redwood): understood — we'll push our SOC2 and pen test summary. breach notification 72 hours is in our standard commitments but we'll annotate it.
[03:07] Anya (Sable): procurement will also need to see cost line items — reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go, egress fees. we got hit by egress previously.
[03:17] Maya (Redwood): yes we can break down the pricing. for Dedicated we do reserved monthly commits with discounted per-token rates; for hosted API it's pay as you go. egress is typically charged for large model artifacts or dataset transfers, we can show how to minimize egress via caching or colocating datasets.
[03:34] Devon (Sable): do you have examples of expected token-costs for inference for a sample 2K sequence? we need numbers for our FinOps approval.
[03:43] Liam (Redwood): we'll put together a token-cost spreadsheet — it depends on model and quantization. for example, a 2K-generation on a 7B quantized model on dedicated looks roughly X tokens per second at Y cost — we'll make that concrete in the pilot plan.
[04:02] Marcus (Sable): can we also get performance SLOs? we need 95th percentile latency under 200ms for interactive flows, otherwise we can't put it in prod.
[04:12] Liam (Redwood): 200ms 95p is tight depending on model and batching. for smaller models and dedicated pools it's achievable; for large llms at 2K context it's less likely. we can propose fallbacks — use a smaller low-latency model for interactive and a larger one for heavy generation.
[04:32] Priya (Sable): about rollouts — procurement wants a staged rollout and a canary with rollback controls. does Redwood provide canary and A/B?
[04:40] Maya (Redwood): yes, rollouts are supported in Console — canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to a cheaper or older model if errors spike. we'll demo that in the technical onboarding session.
[04:53] Anya (Sable): timeline wise: procurement wants to approve pricing by end of next week. legal needs MSA redlines by mid-next week. security wants a pilot by 6/15. is that realistic?
[05:06] Maya (Redwood): we can aim for that. action items: we'll share the MSA + DPA today or tomorrow with annotations. SE team will prepare pilot plan and pricing spreadsheet.
[05:18] Devon (Sable): about data residency — are there regional controls to keep model artifacts in EU vs US? we operate in both.
[05:27] Liam (Redwood): yes, deployments can be regional; you can pin a model to a region. if you run private in your VPC in eu-west, everything stays there. hosted API might be routed to closest region, but for strict residency you want private.
[05:43] Marcus (Sable): compliance question — do you provide audit logs with user-level access entries? we need to show who accessed what prompt and when.
[05:52] Liam (Redwood): audit logs are available; retention is configurable for enterprise plans. some entries can be redacted by default for privacy; for your case we can keep user-level access logs in the private deployment and export them to your SIEM.
[06:07] Priya (Sable): what about data deletion and right-to-be-forgotten requests? we need contractual guarantees.
[06:14] Maya (Redwood): we support request flows and deletion hooks; for private you'd control the data store, for hosted we have deletion processes tied to customer tenant. we'll annotate contractual language.
[06:24] Anya (Sable): pricing — egress again. if we set up a private VPC peering, does that eliminate egress charges?
[06:32] Liam (Redwood): peering can reduce public egress; there are still cross-region transfer considerations. we'll show a cost comparison.
[06:41] Maya (Redwood): ok, any blockers from legal now?
[06:44] Priya (Sable): I'd like to mark two DPA clauses non-negotiable: data residency plus audit access. also need clarity on subprocessors.
[06:53] Maya (Redwood): we'll label subprocessors and provide list and options for limited subprocessors under the DPA; can you confirm preferred retention windows?
[07:01] Priya (Sable): 12 months for logs, 7 years for audit records in certain regulated contexts — we'll provide exact requirements.
[07:11] Devon (Sable): technical ask — our traffic is bursty, peaking at 600 rps for inference for short periods. we'd like automatic autoscale for reserved pools — how fine grained is your autoscale?
[07:24] Liam (Redwood): autoscale can be configured with thresholds and burst capacity; with Dedicated you get a baseline and can configure burst headroom. we'll include suggested autoscale policy for your traffic pattern in the pilot plan.
[07:38] Anya (Sable): procurement will need a clean pricing line that separates monthly commit, burst overage, and egress. also want a term for credits if uptime dips below SLA.
[07:48] Maya (Redwood): we can show SLA tiers with credits and latency objectives. credit formulas are in the SLA; we'll highlight that for you.
[07:57] Marcus (Sable): are pen test reports current? we need a recent one within last 12 months.
[08:03] Maya (Redwood): yes — we'll share the most recent pentest summary and SOC2 Type II report.
[08:10] Priya (Sable): ok, about the pilot: what will success criteria be? we need clear pass/fail signals for procurement sign off.
[08:19] Liam (Redwood): propose success criteria: 95p latency under agreed threshold for X workload, error rate under 0.5%, cost per 1k tokens under target, ability to onboard into your VPC and KMS without released payload telemetry.
[08:36] Devon (Sable): can we do an initial smoke benchmark internally with a small dataset to sanity-check before full pilot?
[08:42] Liam (Redwood): yes — we can provide a runbook and a small test harness.
[08:48] Anya (Sable): procurement note — we'll likely ask for a short-term commercial grace for the pilot (discounted reserved for first month) to make internal signoff easier.
[08:58] Maya (Redwood): that is typical — we'll propose pilot pricing and a path to reserved commit discounts.
[09:04] Priya (Sable): another legal ask — can you add a clause that requires market-competitive indemnity for model hallucination harms? we need to be careful.
[09:15] Maya (Redwood): we'll flag indemnity and model risk language for legal to review; some customers negotiate carve-outs, we'll surface options.
[09:24] Marcus (Sable): competitor check — BigCloud AI said they'd host in our VPC but had higher egress fees; VaultAI offered BYOK but slower latency. we're comparing.
[09:36] Maya (Redwood): understood — we'll try to show a differentiated breakdown: latency, cost, and operational controls.
[09:45] Liam (Redwood): quick technical thing — for caching we support prefix/KV caching to reduce repeated token costs. if your workload has repetition it helps cut cost.
[09:58] Devon (Sable): good. we'll send sample logs to show repetition.
[10:03] Anya (Sable): procurement needs the annotated MSA to route to finance; can you get that in two days?
[10:09] Maya (Redwood): yes, we'll circulate annotated MSA + DPA tomorrow morning.
[10:15] Priya (Sable): can you include a table of subcontractors and where they operate?
[10:20] Liam (Redwood): yes — we'll include the subprocessors list and region mapping.
[10:26] Maya (Redwood): ok i'll recap next steps at the end. any other burning questions?
[10:31] Marcus (Sable): one more — are there options for on-prem if VPC isn't sufficient? some of our data centers are air-gapped.
[10:39] Liam (Redwood): we offer an on-prem package for air-gapped environments — that's a more involved integration but available for enterprise licensing. we can discuss separately.
[10:50] Priya (Sable): great, thanks.

[32:12] (Note: meeting advanced, skipped some small asides)

[32:20] Maya (Redwood): quick recap of action items — we'll send: redlined MSA+DPA, SOC2 and pen test summary, subprocessors list, and pilot benchmark plan. Sable to send: DPA non-negotiables, traffic profile, and list of ciphers/KMS requirements. SE to schedule technical workshop.
[32:46] Anya (Sable): procurement will expect pilot pricing and committed discount proposal by 6/05.
[32:53] Maya (Redwood): we'll aim for that.

[41:10] Maya (Redwood): thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with doc links and propose the working session times.
[41:20] Marcus (Sable): thanks, bye.
[41:25] Priya (Sable): thanks.
[41:30] Devon (Sable): bye.
[41:33] Liam (Redwood): bye all.

End of transcript. Some transcription artifacts present (names and acronyms may be slightly off).
